title: Semantic Similarity Analytics
summary: Analyze semantic neighborhoods to find retrieval gaps, repeated intents, and content drift without treating vector distance as an objective truth score.
overview: Semantic similarity analytics uses embedding relationships to study how queries, documents, answers, or feedback cluster and change. It can reveal duplicate knowledge, underserved query groups, unusual incoming topics, and mismatches between questions and retrieved evidence. The representation reflects the embedding model’s training and preprocessing, so observed distance is model-dependent.

Similarity is neither factual correctness nor causal explanation. A wrong answer can be semantically close to a correct one, and opposite statements can share vocabulary. Analytics should combine vector signals with labeled outcomes, source coverage, and aggregate operational metrics. Keep model versions stable within a comparison or explicitly align and rebaseline the analysis.

production.poc: A prototype visualizes a small labeled query set and checks whether neighborhoods correspond to useful task distinctions.
production.production: Production links aggregate similarity patterns to retrieval outcomes, uses approved data retention, and validates alert thresholds.
production.scale: Enterprise scale monitors drift by language and task, maintains representation lineage, and avoids turning exploratory clusters into unsupported individual-level judgments.

components.name: Governed sample collector
components.role: Selects approved queries or document representations with minimal identifying data.

components.name: Embedding pipeline
components.role: Creates versioned vectors using consistent preprocessing.

components.name: Neighborhood and clustering analysis
components.role: Finds recurring intents, outliers, and content overlap.

components.name: Outcome joiner
components.role: Connects patterns to retrieval recall, unsupported answers, or escalation rates.

components.name: Review workflow
components.role: Lets domain owners validate findings before changing routing or content.

flow.title: Define the analytic question
flow.description: Choose a concrete goal such as missing knowledge coverage or duplicate content.

flow.title: Collect an approved sample
flow.description: Apply retention and access rules and retain representation provenance.

flow.title: Compute comparable vectors
flow.description: Use one compatible embedding configuration for the analyzed population.

flow.title: Find patterns
flow.description: Calculate neighborhoods or clusters and inspect representative examples.

flow.title: Validate with outcomes
flow.description: Check whether the pattern corresponds to actual task failures or useful content gaps.

flow.title: Act and remeasure
flow.description: Update knowledge or retrieval configuration, then compare the affected task slice against its baseline.

useCase.title: Finding missing help-center content
useCase.situation: A university assistant handles questions about enrollment, facilities, and administrative processes.
useCase.problem: Many unanswered queries use varied wording, making simple keyword reports hard to interpret.
useCase.requirement: Identify recurring unmet information needs without profiling individual students.
useCase.architecture: An approved aggregate sample is embedded, clustered, and joined to unresolved-answer outcomes.
runtime: A cluster of differently worded facility-access questions shows poor evidence coverage.
Service owners review representative anonymized examples and add the missing authoritative guidance.
useCase.failure: If a model update changes the cluster geometry, the analytics baseline is rebuilt before declaring a sudden topic shift.
useCase.impact: Measure supported-answer improvement in the affected cluster, sample coverage, and review accuracy; visually separated clusters do not prove meaningful business categories.

tradeoffs.cost: Produces clusters that may lack operational meaning.
Requires reliable task metrics and joins.
Can distort distances and should not be treated as quantitative proof.

failures.scenario: Embedding upgrade looks like demand drift
failures.detection: Neighborhood changes occur without corresponding query changes.

failures.recovery: Use labeled contradiction and factual-support checks.

mistakes.fix: Inspect representative examples and validate outcomes.

whenToUse: Use for knowledge-gap discovery and retrieval diagnostics.
Use when findings can be validated against outcomes.
whenNotToUse: Avoid unsupported sensitive profiling of individuals.
Do not use similarity alone to approve factual answers.
checklist: Join similarity signals to real outcomes.
